title: Atomic Theory and Experimental Evidence
purpose: Explain how evidence changed atomic models over time.
safetyNotes: Use diagrams, historical data, and simulations only. No radiation or particle experiments are performed.
simulationReview: Direct simulation/resource link is provided in P01.html and in directSimulationUrl.
assessmentStimulusNeeded: Atomic model timeline and model/evidence table
simulationVirtualLabReviewRequirement: Required for atomic models, periodic trends, energy levels, and spectra
directSimulationStudentTask: After the simulation opens, start with the atom model shown on the screen and turn on alpha-particle firing if it is not already moving. Observe several alpha particles and separate their paths into mostly straight, slightly deflected, or strongly deflected. Switch or compare available atom-model views if the simulation provides more than one model. Record which observation supports a small dense nucleus and one limitation of the model for the lesson focus: Atomic Theory and Experimental Evidence.
simulationReviewImplementation: Student-facing lesson includes one exact direct simulation/resource link plus adjacent step-by-step directions for what to open, click/use, observe, record, and connect to the lesson standard.
simulationSourceReference: OpenStax Chemistry 2e; PhET Rutherford Scattering; CK-12
